Physics Based Meta-heuristic Approaches in Solving Design and Manufacturing Problems

Abstract:

The present study aims at improving the exploration-exploitation trade-off in GSA for unconstrained, constrained, multi-objective, and combinatorial (flexible job-shop
scheduling) optimization problems. For unconstrained optimization, the present study measures the diversity values of two consecutive iterations. If the change in diversity values
is insignificant, disruption is performed using a sigmoid function. To overcome the limitations of CGSA, chaotic sequences are used only during the exploration stage, and
gradual exploitation is provided by the sigmoid function in the later part of the search. The proposed algorithm is called diversity-based chaotic GSA (DCGSA). DCGSA is tested on
twenty-eight benchmarks and eleven unconstrained machining problems. DCGSA outperforms GSA, CGSA, and different variants of GSA for unconstrained benchmark
problems and machining problems. However, many real-world problems are subjected to inequality and equality constraints, in addition to lower and upper bounds on decision
variables. Therefore, a constraint handling mechanism is required to enable DCGSA for solving constrained optimization problems. The present study incorporates a parameterless
constraint-handling mechanism, known as feasibility rules, to make DCGSA suitable for constrained optimization problems. The proposed algorithm for constrained optimization is
tested on sixty one benchmark problems, seventeen real-world constrained design problems, and seven constrained machining problems. The proposed algorithm outperformed GSA
and CGSA on benchmark functions, along with real-world design and machining problems.
A dual population gravitational search algorithm with guided exploration (DPGSAGE) is proposed for multi-objective problems (MOPs) and multimodal multi-objective problems (MMOPs). In the proposed approach, the population is divided into two subpopulations based on fitness values obtained from the non-domination relation and ranking method according to the strength of the solution.
Subpopulation 1 performs mutation based on the overall and local diversity values to identify multiple Pareto sets.&nbsp&nbspFor the flexible job shop scheduling problem (FJSSP), the GSA and CGSA are initially
mapped to solve it using a real-number-based encoding and decoding mechanism. The corresponding algorithms are named the real-coded gravitational search algorithm (RGSA)
and the real-coded chaotic gravitational search algorithm (RCGSA). The operators of the GSA and CGSA report inferior solutions for the FJSSP. Therefore, the present work
proposes a discrete GSA, known as the permutation enhanced gravitational search algorithm (PEGSA), to overcome the limitations of RGSA and RCGSA..
